extracted.intended_audience: readers, advertisers, press, potential job applicants, and people seeking to contact or license material from The Onion
extracted.subtask_description: The Onion 'About' page describing the publication’s mission, history, editorial practices, contact points, and policies (submission, licensing, advertising, privacy, employment, and legal). Serves as authoritative guidance on how outsiders should interact with the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited electronic communications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited bulk email, email attachments, and junk email of any kind are not accepted, and will be filtered and immediately discarded upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send unsolicited bulk messages or attachments; they will be ignored. Use the specified contact addresses for appropriate inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission policy — no outside submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No, The Onion does not accept outside submissions of any kind. We will not respond to any unsolicited submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send articles, ideas, pitches, or other creative submissions; they will not be considered or acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment application policy — do not send unsolicited résumés
rubrics_metrics.description: Onion Inc. regularly posts new openings on the Careers section of our website. Please do not send résumés unless specifically told to do so in a job listing. Any unsolicited résumés will be immediately discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the Careers page for openings and follow application instructions there rather than emailing résumés unsolicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback policy and response limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all concerns to publicfeedback@theonion.com. The Onion cannot guarantee a response to any feedback to its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the public feedback address for article concerns, but expect that not all contacts will receive a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal position on satire and lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not do that. The First Amendment protects satire as a form of free speech and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion asserts constitutional protection for satire when responding to threats of litigation; this is their stated legal posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of names in stories — invented names policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion uses invented names in all of its stories, except in cases where public figures are being satirized. Any other use of real names is accidental and coincidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial practice is to avoid using real private individuals' names; real names appear only when satirizing public figures or by accident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion is not intended for readers under 18 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content is aimed at adults; minors are not the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy policy reference
rubrics_metrics.description: To read The Onion’s privacy policy, please click here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed privacy practices are provided via the linked privacy policy; readers should consult that page for data-handling specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising inquiry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all advertising inquiries to advertising@theonion.com. Please specify the business you would like to advertise, and the appropriate advertising sales representative will get back to you promptly. For more information regarding advertising opportunities with The Onion, please consult our Media Kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct advertising requests to the advertising address and include business details; consult the Media Kit for options and specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press/coverage inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m a member of a lesser media organization and I want to cover The Onion. Please send all inquiries to press@g-omedia.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media requests about The Onion should be sent to the press email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking engagements procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The writers and editors ... are available for speaking engagements ... Please send all inquiries to press@g-omedia.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the press address to request appearances by writers/editors; include event details and nature of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website support/technical issue reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: To report a technical issue with TheOnion.com, please submit a request through the Kinja support center with a summary of the issue and your browser information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear summary and browser details via the Kinja support portal for technical problems; do not use editorial or advertising addresses for technical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive access and content licensing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: This website contains all of The Onion’s articles published from early 1996 through the present. You can browse by topic, tags, and authors or search the entire archive by keyword. Please send requests for articles and graphics from past issues, including those from before 1996, to permissions@theonion.com. The Onion will attempt to answer your query but cannot guarantee a response to all such requests. The Onion may not be reprinted or retransmitted in whole or in part without the express written consent of the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archived material is browsable online for most years; licensing, reprint, and requests for past materials must go to the permissions address and require written consent. Responses are not guaranteed.
